articles.title: Diwali Gift Guide: Best Instax Instant Cameras On Amazon, From Rs 6,999, And What Each Print Costs
articles.description: Instant cameras are one of the easiest Diwali gifts to get right: you hand over a camera, and the first photo is in the recipient's hand within minutes. With Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 live, Fujifilm's Instax range is listed from Rs 6,999. Here is a price list and a guide to the one number most buyers forget, the cost of each print. Instax Camera Prices On Amazon Amazon's listings show the following prices, which can change during the sale: Instax Mini 12: Rs 6,999 (listed MRP varies by colour, from Rs 7,499 to Rs 8,999). It has auto exposure, a selfie mirror and a close-up mode, and runs on two AA batteries. Instax Mini 12 Gift Box with 10 shots: Rs 7,499. Instax Mini 13: Rs 7,999 in Clay White, the newer model of the Mini 12. Instax Mini 41: Rs 10,499 against an MRP of Rs 13,999, a 25 per cent discount. Instax Wide 400: listed from Rs 14,499, for larger wide-format prints. Prices vary by colour and seller, so the same camera can cost a little less in one shade than in another. Compare listings before you pick a colour. The Real Cost Is The Film The camera is a one-time cost, but every print needs film. A single pack of 10 Instax Mini sheets is listed at Rs 699, against an MRP of Rs 799, and a 20-shot pack at Rs 1,399, which works out to about Rs 70 per print. A 20-print pack lasts a family gathering, so a gift box with only 10 shots can run out within an evening. If you are gifting a camera, add at least one or two extra film packs, and check the date on the pack, since instant film has a shelf life and works best when fresh. Keep unexposed film away from heat. Which Model Suits Which Person The Mini 12 and Mini 13 suit teenagers, first-time users and anyone who wants a simple point-and-shoot with automatic exposure. If you do not need the newer model, the Mini 12 at Rs 6,999 saves Rs 1,000 over the Mini 13. The Mini 41 costs more and is aimed at buyers who want a step up from the entry models. The Wide 400 makes larger prints, which suit group photos and travel scenes, though its film generally costs more. Instant cameras give you a physical keepsake but offer far less control than a mirrorless camera or a phone, so they work best as a fun extra and not as someone's only camera. If the recipient wants to learn photography seriously, an entry-level mirrorless camera such as Canon's EOS R100, listed at Rs 44,989, is a better long-term gift. Make It A Complete Gift Add an album or photo frame, a pack of AA batteries and a spare film pack. Some listings sell gift boxes that bundle extras, but compare the bundle price against buying the pieces separately, since bundles can include items you will not use. Keep the receipt and the invoice with the gift, in case of warranty or exchange needs. Check The Offer Before You Pay Amazon has confirmed a 10 per cent instant discount on eligible SBI credit and debit cards, with caps and minimum order values, so check whether your cart value qualifies. Check that the listing is for a new, sealed camera sold by an authorised seller, whether batteries and film are included, and the return window, since gifts sometimes need exchanging. You can browse instant cameras and other cameras on Amazon and explore camera gifts and accessories, then compare the final payable amount before you order.

articles.title: Playing PS5 Or Xbox On A New TV? Best Gaming TV Deals In Amazon's Festive Sale, From Rs 35,499
articles.description: Many TVs in Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 advertise gaming features, but the labels can be misleading. A "120Hz" sticker may describe a true 120Hz panel or a motion-processing feature on a 60Hz panel, and the difference matters if you play on a PS5, Xbox or gaming PC. With the sale live, here is a plain guide to what the specifications mean and which deals we could confirm. Native Refresh Rate Versus Marketing Labels Refresh rate is how many times the screen updates each second. A native 120Hz or 144Hz panel can show smoother motion in fast games, provided your console or PC can output that frame rate. Some TVs instead have a native 60Hz panel and add a feature such as a 120Hz game accelerator or motion interpolation, which can reduce blur but does not turn the panel into a true 120Hz display. TCL's 75-inch 75T6C, for instance, is listed with a native 60Hz panel and MEMC, plus a 120Hz Game Accelerator, while the TCL 55T8D QD-Mini LED is listed with a native 144Hz panel. Always look for the word "native" on the listing or in the specifications, and check which HDMI ports support the higher rates. Features That Matter Besides Refresh Rate Variable refresh rate, or VRR, keeps the picture smooth when frame rates fluctuate. Auto low latency mode, or ALLM, switches the TV to its fastest game setting when a console is detected. HGiG helps games display HDR correctly. Samsung lists ALLM, VRR and HGiG on its 55-inch Crystal 4K model, and LG's OLED evo C5 supports VRR up to 144Hz. Input lag, the delay between pressing a button and seeing the result, is rarely printed on listings, so read reviews that measure it. Finally, count the HDMI ports: the TCL 55T8D has four, which helps if you connect a console, a soundbar and a set-top box. Gaming TV Deals We Could Confirm Prices below were reported on or around October 8 to 13 and can change as the sale runs. Xiaomi 55-inch Smartchoice FX Pro (120Hz): Rs 35,499, against an original price of Rs 62,999. TCL 55T8D QD-Mini LED (native 144Hz, up to 288Hz with DLG): Rs 57,990, against an MRP of Rs 89,990. TCL 65-inch 4K QLED with Game Master: Rs 58,990, down from Rs 1,14,990. TCL 75-inch 75T6C QLED (native 60Hz with 120Hz Game Accelerator): Rs 61,990 including bank discounts, against a usual price of Rs 76,990. LG 65-inch OLED evo C5 (120Hz with VRR up to 144Hz): Rs 1,73,990. Match The TV To Your Console And Room Match the TV to your setup. A PS5 or Xbox Series X can output 4K at 120Hz in supported games, but only through an HDMI port that supports it, so check the port labels. For casual or cricket-and-streaming households, a native 60Hz set with good HDR and sound is enough, and you can save the money. For a bright room, a Mini LED or QLED panel handles glare better than most OLEDs, while OLED suits dark-room, single-player gaming. Size also matters: a 55-inch set suits a desk or sofa two metres away, while 65 inches suits a larger room. Check The Offer Before You Pay Gaming sets are large purchases, so confirm the exact model number, HDMI port details and warranty before ordering, and check that installation is included. Amazon has confirmed a 10 per cent instant discount on eligible SBI credit and debit cards, with caps and minimum order values, and No Cost EMI is available on many TVs. A discount quoted against a very high "original price" is not a reliable guide, so compare the final payable amount across a few models. You can check gaming and smart TV deals on Amazon and explore more 4K TVs on Amazon before you decide.
